cues.en: Hi. This video is kind of a response to various comments that I've got over the years, ever since that video on Computerphile, where I was describing the sort of problems that we might have when we have a powerful artificial general intelligence with goals which aren't the same as our goals, even if those goals seem pretty benign. We used this thought experiment of an extremely powerful AGI working to optimize the simple goal of collecting stamps, and some of the problems that that might cause.
cues.zh: 嗨。这个视频算是对我多年来收到的一些评论的回应，尤其是自从我在 Computerphile 上做了那期视频之后。当时我描述了：当我们拥有一个强大的通用人工智能，而它的目标与我们的目标不一致时，可能会遇到哪些问题，即便那些目标看起来相当无害。我们用了这样一个思想实验：一个极其强大的 AGI 致力于优化收集邮票这个简单目标，以及这可能引发的一些问题。

cues.en: I got some comments from people saying that they think the stamp collecting device is stupid, and not that it's a stupid thought experiment, but the device itself is actually stupid. They said unless it has complex goals, or the ability to choose its own goals, then it didn't count as being highly intelligent. On other videos I got comments saying it takes intelligence to do moral reasoning, so an intelligent AGI system should be able to do that, and a super-intelligent should be able to do it better than humans. In fact, if a super-intelligence decides that the right thing to do is to kill us all,
cues.zh: 我收到一些人的评论，说他们觉得这个集邮装置很蠢——不是说这个思想实验很蠢，而是这个装置本身实际上很蠢。他们说，除非它有复杂的目标，或者有能力选择自己的目标，否则它就不能算高度智能。在其他视频里，我也收到评论说，道德推理需要智能，所以一个智能的 AGI 系统应该能做到这一点，而超级智能应该能比人类做得更好。事实上，如果一个超级智能判定，正确的做法是把我们全部杀掉，

cues.en: then I guess that's the right thing to do. These comments are all kind of suffering from the same mistake, which is what this video is about. But before I get to that, I need to lay some groundwork first. If you like Occam's razor, then you'll love Hume's guillotine, also called the Izzord problem. This is a pretty simple concept that I'd like to be better known. The idea is, statements can be divided up into two types. Izz statements.
cues.zh: 那我想那就是正确的事。这些评论都或多或少犯了同一个错误，而这就是本视频要讲的。但在进入正题之前，我需要先打点基础。如果你喜欢奥卡姆剃刀，那你会喜欢休谟断头台，也叫实然-应然问题。这个概念很简单，我希望它更广为人知。这个想法是：陈述可以分为两类。实然陈述。

cues.en: and ought statements. These statements, or positive statements, are statements about how the world is, how the world was in the past, how the world will be in the future, or how the world would be in hypothetical situations. This is facts about the nature of reality, the causal relationships between things, that kind of thing. Then you have the ought statements, the should statements, the normative statements. These are about the way the world should be, the way we want the world to be. Statements about our goals, our values,
cues.zh: 以及应然陈述。这些陈述，或者说实证陈述，是关于世界现在如何、过去如何、未来将如何，或者在假设情境下会如何的陈述。这是关于现实本质的事实、事物之间的因果关系之类的东西。然后是应然陈述、应该陈述、规范性陈述。这些是关于世界应该怎样、我们希望世界怎样的陈述。关于我们的目标、我们的价值观的陈述，

cues.en: Ethics, morals, what we want, all of that stuff. Now, you can derive logical statements from one another. Like, it's snowing outside, that's an is statement. It's cold when it snows, another is statement. And then you can deduce, therefore it's cold outside. That's another is statement, it's our conclusion. This is all pretty obvious. But, you might say something like, it's snowing outside, therefore you ought to put on a coat. And that's a very normal sort of sentence that people might say. But as a logical statement,
cues.zh: 伦理、道德、我们想要什么，诸如此类。现在，你可以从一些陈述逻辑地推导出另一些陈述。比如，外面在下雪，这是一个实然陈述。下雪时很冷，这是另一个实然陈述。然后你可以推出：所以外面很冷。这又是一个实然陈述，这是我们的结论。这些都挺显然的。但你可能会说类似这样的话：外面在下雪，所以你应该穿件外套。这是人们可能会说的一种很正常的句子。但作为一个逻辑陈述，

cues.en: It actually relies on some hidden assumptions. Without assuming some kind of ought statement, you can't derive another ought statement. This is the core of the is-ought problem. You can never derive an ought statement using only is statements. You ought to put on a coat. Why? Because it's snowing outside. So why does the fact that it's snowing mean I should put on a coat? Well, the fact that it's snowing means that it's cold. And why should it being cold mean I should put on a coat? If it's cold and you go outside without a coat, you'll be cold. Should I not be cold?
cues.zh: 它实际上依赖于一些隐藏假设。如果不假设某种应然陈述，你就无法推导出另一个应然陈述。这就是实然-应然问题的核心。你永远不能仅用实然陈述推导出应然陈述。你应该穿件外套。为什么？因为外面在下雪。那么，外面在下雪这个事实，为什么意味着我应该穿件外套？嗯，下雪这个事实意味着很冷。那很冷为什么就应该意味着我要穿外套？如果很冷，你不穿外套出门，你就会冷。我不应该冷吗？

cues.en: Well, if you get too cold, you'll freeze to death. Okay, you're saying I shouldn't freeze to death? That was kind of silly. But you see what I'm saying. You can keep laying out is statements for as long as you want. You will never be able to derive that you ought to put on a code. At some point, in order to derive that ought statement, you need to assume at least one other ought statement. If you have some kind of ought statement like
cues.zh: 好吧，如果你太冷，就会冻死。行，你是说我不应该冻死？这听起来有点傻。但你明白我的意思。你可以随心所欲地不断列举各种“实然”陈述。但你永远推导不出你“应当”穿上外套。在某个节点上，为了推导出一个“应然”陈述，你必须先假设至少存在另一个“应然”陈述。如果你有某种应然陈述，比如……

cues.en: I ought to continue to be alive. You can then say, given that I ought to keep living, and that if I go outside without a coat I'll die, then I ought to put on a coat. But unless you have at least one ought statement, you cannot derive any other ought statements. Is statements and ought statements are separated by Hume's guillotine. OK, so people are saying that a device that single-mindedly collects stamps at the cost of everything else is stupid and doesn't count as a powerful intelligence. So let's define our terms. What is intelligence?
cues.zh: “我应当继续活着”。那你就可以说，既然我应当活着，而且不穿外套出门就会死，那么我就应当穿上外套。但除非你至少先有一个应然陈述，否则你无法推导出任何其他应然陈述。实然陈述和应然陈述被“休谟断头台”所隔开。好，有人说，一个不惜一切代价、一心只收集邮票的设备很蠢，算不上强大的智能。那我们先来明确一下定义。什么是智能？

cues.en: And conversely, what is stupidity? I feel like I made fairly clear in those videos what I meant by intelligence. We're talking about AGI systems as intelligent agents, they're entities that take actions in the world in order to achieve their goals or maximise their utility functions. Intelligence is the thing that allows them to choose good actions, to choose actions that will get them what they want.
cues.zh: 反过来，什么又是愚蠢？我觉得在之前的视频里，我已经把智能的含义讲得很清楚了。我们把 AGI 系统视为智能体，它们是在现实世界中采取行动，以实现目标或最大化效用函数的实体。智能就是让它们能做出良好决策、选择能达成目的之行动的能力。

cues.en: An agent's level of intelligence really means its level of effectiveness at pursuing its goals. In practice, this is likely to involve having or building an accurate model of reality, keeping that model up to date by reasoning about observations, and using the model to make predictions about the future, and the likely consequences of different possible actions, to figure out which actions will result in which outcomes. Intelligence involves answering questions like, what is the world like? How does it work? What will happen next? What would happen in this scenario or that scenario?
cues.zh: 一个智能体的智能水平，实质上是指它追求目标的有效程度。在实践中，这通常涉及拥有或构建一个精准的现实模型，通过对观察结果进行推理来持续更新该模型，并利用该模型预测未来以及不同行动的潜在后果，从而搞清楚哪些行动会导致哪些结果。智能涉及回答这些问题：世界是什么样的？它是如何运作的？接下来会发生什么？在这种或那种场景下会发生什么？

cues.en: What would happen if I took this action or that action? More intelligent systems are in some sense better at answering these kinds of questions, which allows them to be better at choosing actions. But one thing you might notice about these questions is, they're all IS questions. The system has goals, which can be thought of as ought statements, but the level of intelligence depends only on the ability to reason about IS questions in order to answer the single ought question, what action should I take next? So given that that's what we mean by intelligence, what does it mean to be stupid?
cues.zh: 如果我采取这个或那个行动，会发生什么？更具智能的系统在某种意义上更擅长回答这类问题，从而能更好地做出行动抉择。但关于这些问题，你可能会注意到一点：它们全是“实然”问题。系统拥有目标，这可以被视为应然陈述，但其智能水平完全取决于对实然问题的推理能力，以此来回答唯一的应然问题——“我下一步应该采取什么行动？”所以，既然智能是这个意思，那愚蠢又意味着什么呢？

cues.en: Well, firstly, you can be stupid in terms of those is questions. For example, by building a model that doesn't correspond with reality, or by failing to update your model properly with new evidence. If I look out of my window, and I see there's snow everywhere, and I see a snowman, and I think to myself, oh, what a beautiful, warm, sunny day. Then that's stupid, right? My belief is wrong, and I had all the clues to realize it's cold outside. So beliefs can be stupid by not corresponding to reality.
cues.zh: 首先，你可以在那些“实然”问题上犯蠢。比如，建一个不符合现实的模型，或者没有根据新证据正确更新你的模型。如果我往窗外看，看到到处都是雪，还看到一个雪人，然后心里想：哦，多么美好、温暖、阳光明媚的一天。那这就是蠢，对吧？我的信念是错的，而且我本来有所有线索能意识到外面很冷。所以，信念可以因为不符合现实而犯蠢。

cues.en: What about actions? Like, if I go outside in the snow without my coat, that's stupid, right? Well, it might be. If I think it's sunny and warm and I go outside to sunbathe, then yeah, that's stupid. But if I just came out of a sauna or something and I'm too hot and I want to cool myself down, then going outside without a coat might be quite sensible. You can't know if an action is stupid just by looking at its consequences. You have to also know the goals of the agent taking the action. You can't just use is statements, you need an ought. So actions are only stupid relative to a particular goal.
cues.zh: 那行动呢？比如，我不穿外套就走进雪里，这很蠢，对吧？嗯，也许是。如果我以为外面阳光温暖，就出去晒太阳，那确实很蠢。但如果我刚从桑拿房出来之类，太热了想凉快一下，那不穿外套出门可能相当明智。你不能只看后果就知道一个行动蠢不蠢。你还得知道采取行动的行动者的目标。你不能只用“实然”陈述，你需要“应然”。所以，行动只有在相对于特定目标时才是蠢的。

cues.en: It doesn't feel that way, though. People often talk about actions being stupid without specifying what goals they're stupid relative to. But in those cases, the goals are implied. We're humans, and when we say that an action is stupid in normal human communication, we're making some assumptions about normal human goals. And because we're always talking about people and people tend to want similar things, it's sort of a shorthand that we can skip what goals we're talking about. So what about the goals, then? Can goals be stupid?
cues.zh: 不过，感觉并非如此。人们常谈某个行动很蠢，却不说明它是相对于什么目标而蠢。但在这些情况下，目标是隐含的。我们是人类，在日常人类交流中说一个行动很蠢时，我们对正常人类目标做了一些假设。而且因为我们总在谈论人，而人往往想要相似的东西，所以这算是一种简写，可以跳过我们在谈什么目标。那么目标呢？目标可以蠢吗？

cues.en: Well, this depends on the difference between instrumental goals and terminal goals. This is something I've covered elsewhere, but your terminal goals are the things that you want just because you want them. You don't have a particular reason to want them, they're just what you want. The instrumental goals are the goals you want because they'll get you closer to your terminal goals. Like, if I have a terminal goal to visit a town that's far away...
cues.zh: 这取决于工具性目标和终极目标之间的区别。这个我在别处讲过，但你的终极目标就是你仅仅因为想要而想要的东西。你没有一个特定理由去想要它们，它们就是你想要的东西。工具性目标是你想要的目标，因为它们会让你更接近终极目标。比如，如果我有一个终极目标是去一个很远的小镇……

cues.en: Maybe an instrumental goal would be to find a train station. I don't want to find a train station just because trains are cool. I want to find a train as a means to an end. It's going to take me to this town. So that makes it an instrumental goal. Now, an instrumental goal can be stupid if I want to go to this distant town so I decide I want to find a pogo stick. That's pretty stupid. Finding a pogo stick is a stupid instrumental goal if my terminal goal is to get to a faraway place. But if my terminal goal was something else, like having fun, it might not be stupid.
cues.zh: 那么一个工具性目标可能是找到火车站。我并不是因为火车很酷才想找火车站。我想找到火车作为达到目的的手段。它会带我去这个小镇。所以这使它成为工具性目标。现在，如果一个工具性目标是：我想去这个遥远的小镇，所以我决定要找一根弹簧单高跷，那它就可能很蠢。那相当蠢。如果我的终极目标是去一个很远的地方，那么找弹簧单高跷就是一个愚蠢的工具性目标。但如果我的终极目标是别的，比如玩得开心，那它可能就不蠢。

cues.en: So in that way, it's like actions. Instrumental goals can only be stupid relative to terminal goals. So you see how this works. Beliefs and predictions can be stupid relative to evidence or relative to reality. Actions can be stupid relative to goals of any kind. Instrumental goals can be stupid relative to terminal goals. But here's the big point. Terminal goals can't be stupid. There's nothing to judge them against.
cues.zh: 从这个角度看，它就像行动。工具性目标只能是相对于终极目标而言的愚蠢。所以你明白这个逻辑了吧。信念和预测可以是相对于证据或现实而言愚蠢的。行动可以是相对于任何目标而言愚蠢的。工具性目标可以是相对于终极目标而言愚蠢的。但关键点来了：终极目标不可能愚蠢。没有任何标准可以用来评判它们。

cues.en: If a terminal goal seems stupid, like let's say collecting stamps seems like a stupid terminal goal, that's because it would be stupid as an instrumental goal to human terminal goals. But the stamp collector does not have human terminal goals. Similarly, the things that humans care about would seem stupid to the stamp collector because they result in so few stamps. So let's get back to those comments. One type of comment says...
cues.zh: 如果一个终极目标看起来很愚蠢，比如收集邮票听起来像个愚蠢的终极目标，那是因为作为人类终极目标的工具性目标，它确实是愚蠢的。但集邮者并没有人类的终极目标。同样，人类在乎的东西在集邮者看来也会很愚蠢，因为这些东西带来的邮票太少了。那么回到那些评论。有一类评论说……

cues.en: This behaviour of just single-mindedly going after one thing and ignoring everything else, and ignoring the totally obvious fact that stamps aren't that important, is really stupid behaviour. You're calling this thing a superintelligence, but it doesn't seem superintelligent to me, it just seems kind of like an idiot.
cues.zh: 这种只顾一门心思追逐一个东西、无视其他一切、无视“邮票其实没那么重要”这个显而易见的事实的行为，实在是太蠢了。你把这东西称为超级智能，但它在我看来一点也不超级智能，倒像是个白痴。

cues.en: Hopefully the answer to this is now clear. The Stamp Collector's actions are stupid relative to human goals, but it doesn't have human goals. Its intelligence comes not from its goals, but from its ability to understand and reason about the world, allowing it to choose actions that achieve its goals. And this is true whatever those goals actually are. Some people commented along the lines of, well, okay, yeah, sure, you've defined intelligence to only include this type of is statement kind of reasoning. But I don't like that definition. I think, to be truly intelligent,
cues.zh: 希望现在的答案已经很清楚了。集邮者的行动相对于人类目标是愚蠢的，但它并没有人类的目标。它的智能不是来自它的目标，而是来自它理解和推理世界的能力，这让它能够选择能实现目标的行动。而且无论那些目标究竟是什么，这一点都成立。有些人的评论大意是：好吧，行吧，你把智能定义成只包含这种“是陈述”式的推理，但我不喜欢这个定义。我认为，要算真正的智能，

cues.en: you need to have complex goals. Something with simple goals doesn't count as intelligent. To that I say...
cues.zh: 你得有复杂的目标才行。目标简单的东西不算有智能。对此我的回应是……

cues.en: Well, you can use words however you want, I guess. I'm using intelligence here as a technical term in the way that it's often used in the field. You're free to have your own definition of the word, but the fact that something fails to meet your definition of intelligence does not mean that it will fail to behave in a way that most people would call intelligent. If the stamp collector outwits you, gets around everything you've put in its way, and outmaneuvers you mentally, it comes up with new strategies that you would never have thought of to stop you from turning it off and stop you from preventing it from making stamps. And as a consequence, it turns the
cues.zh: 呃，你想怎么用词都行吧。我在这里是把“智能”当作一个技术术语来用的，用的是这个领域的常见用法。你完全可以有自己的定义，但某个东西不符合你对智能的定义，并不意味着它就不会表现出大多数人会称之为智能的行为。如果集邮者智胜了你，绕过了你设置的一切障碍，在心智上比你的策略更高明——它想出了你压根想不到的新策略来阻止你关掉它、阻止你妨碍它造邮票——结果它以你完全无法想象的各种方式把

cues.en: entire world into stamps in various ways you could never think of, it's totally okay for you to say that it doesn't count as intelligent if you want, but you're still dead. I prefer my definition because it better captures the ability to get things done in the world, which is the reason that we actually care about AGI in the first place. Similarly, people who say that in order to be intelligent you need to be able to choose your own goals, I would agree you need to be able to choose your own instrumental goals, but not your own terminal goals.
cues.zh: 整个世界都变成了邮票，那你尽管说它不算智能，但你还是死定了。我更喜欢我的定义，因为它更好地刻画了“在现实中把事情办成”的能力，而这正是我们关心 AGI 的根本原因。同样，那些说“要算智能就得能选择自己的目标”的人，我同意你得能选择自己的工具性目标，但不是选择自己的终极目标。

cues.en: Changing your terminal goals is like willingly taking a pill that will make you want to murder your children. It's something you pretty much never want to do. Apart from some bizarre edge cases, if you rationally want to take an action that changes one of your goals, then that wasn't a terminal goal. Now, moving onto these comments saying an AGI will be able to reason about morality, and if it's really smarter than us, it will actually do moral reasoning better than us. So there's nothing to worry about.
cues.zh: 改变自己的终极目标，就像心甘情愿吞下一颗药，让你想去杀害自己的孩子。这种事你几乎永远不会做。除了一些离奇的边缘情况，如果你理性上想采取某个行动来改变自己的某个目标，那它就不是终极目标。现在看这些评论，说 AGI 能够对道德进行推理，如果它真的比我们更聪明，那它在道德推理上也会比我们做得更好。所以没什么可担心的。

cues.en: It's true that a superior intelligence might be better at moral reasoning than us, but ultimately, moral behaviour depends not on moral reasoning, but on having the right terminal goals. There's a difference between figuring out and understanding human morality, and actually wanting to act according to it. The stamp collecting device has a perfect understanding of human goals, ethics and values, and it uses that only to manipulate people for stamps. Its superhuman moral reasoning doesn't make its actions good.
cues.zh: 更高智能确实可能在道德推理上比我们更强，但最终，道德行为并不取决于道德推理，而取决于是否拥有正确的终极目标。弄清楚并理解人类道德，与真心想按道德行事，是两回事。集邮装置完全理解人类的目标、伦理和价值观，却只用这些来操纵人，为自己收集邮票。它超人般的道德推理并不能让它的行为变好。

cues.en: If we create a superintelligence and it decides to kill us, that doesn't tell us anything about morality, it just means we screwed up. So, what mistake do all of these comments have in common? The orthogonality thesis in AI safety is that more or less any goal is compatible with more or less any level of intelligence, i.e. those properties are orthogonal. You can place them on these two axes, and it's possible to have agents anywhere in this space, anywhere on either scale.
cues.zh: 如果我们造出超级智能，而它决定杀死我们，这并不能说明道德是什么，只能说明我们搞砸了。那么，这些评论共同犯了什么错误？AI 安全中的正交性论点认为，几乎任何目标都能与几乎任何智能水平兼容，也就是说，这两个属性是正交的。你可以把它们放在这两个轴上，而智能体可能出现在这个空间中的任何位置，也就是任一尺度上的任何位置。

cues.en: You can have very weak, low intelligence agents that have complex human-compatible goals. You can have powerful, highly intelligent systems with complex, sophisticated goals. You can have weak, simple agents with silly goals. And yes, you can have powerful, highly intelligent systems with simple, weird, inhuman goals. Any of these are possible, because level of intelligence is about effectiveness at answering is questions. And goals are all about ought questions, and the two sides are separated by Hume's guillotine.
cues.zh: 你可以有非常弱、低智能的智能体，却拥有复杂且与人类兼容的目标。你可以有强大、高智能的系统，拥有复杂、精细的目标。你可以有弱小、简单的智能体，拥有愚蠢的目标。而且没错，你也可以有强大、高智能的系统，拥有简单、古怪、非人类的目标。这些都可能是存在的，因为智能水平关乎有效回答“是什么”的问题，而目标全都关乎“应该怎样”的问题，两边被休谟的铡刀隔开。

cues.en: Hopefully, looking at what we've talked about so far, it should be pretty obvious that this is the case. Like, what would it even mean for it to be false? For it to be impossible to create powerful intelligences with certain goals? The stamp collector is intelligent because it's effective at considering the consequences of sending different combinations of packets on the internet and calculating how many stamps that results in. Exactly how good do you have to be at that?
cues.zh: 希望看到我们到目前为止讨论的内容后，这一点应该相当明显。比如说，它要是假的，究竟意味着什么？意味着不可能创造出带有某些目标的强大智能？集邮器之所以智能，是因为它能有效考虑在互联网上发送不同数据包组合的后果，并计算最终能换来多少邮票。你得在这件事上有多强？

cues.en: before you don't care about stamps anymore and you randomly start to care about some other thing that was never part of your terminal goals, like feeding the hungry or whatever. It's just not going to happen. So that's the orthogonality thesis. It's possible to create a powerful intelligence that will pursue any goal you can specify. Knowing an agent's terminal goals doesn't really tell you anything about its level of intelligence. And knowing an agent's level of intelligence doesn't tell you anything about its goals.
cues.zh: 在你不再关心邮票，转而随机开始关心某个从来不属于你终极目标的东西——比如喂饱饥饿的人之类的——之前，这种事根本不会发生。所以这就是正交性论点。你有可能创造出一种强大智能，去追求你能指定的任何目标。知道一个智能体的终极目标，并不能真正告诉你它的智能水平。而知道一个智能体的智能水平，也不能告诉你它的目标。
